title: You gave more than you could afford… and still felt empty afterward.
paragraphs: You gave more than you could afford… and still felt empty afterward.
No one told you why.
They just said, “Give your 10% or you’re robbing God.” And something in you tightened. Not because you didn’t want to honor God… but because it started to feel like a transaction instead of worship.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

The question isn’t just “Should I tithe?”
The real question is: What does God actually require from you now that Jesus has come?
Because if you miss that… you can give money your whole life and still miss God completely.
Let’s go back.
In the Old Testament, tithing was a command. Clear. Structured. Non-negotiable under the Law. Leviticus 27:30 says, “A tithe of everything from the land… belongs to the Lord; it is holy to the Lord.”
It wasn’t just generosity. It was covenant obedience. Israel was under a system where blessing and curse were tied to law-keeping. You obey—you’re blessed. You disobey—you’re judged.

Then comes Malachi 3:8–10:
“Will a mere mortal rob God? Yet you rob me… in tithes and offerings… Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse…”
Read that again.
This is where most modern teaching stops—and that’s the problem.
Because something happened after Malachi.
Someone came.
And everything changed.
Jesus didn’t just tweak the Law. He fulfilled it.
Matthew 5:17 — “Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets; I have not come to abolish them but to fulfill them.”
That word fulfill isn’t small. It means completion. It means the system that required tithing as a legal obligation was brought to its intended end in Christ.
So now the tension begins.

If tithing was commanded under the Law…
And we are no longer under the Law but under grace (Romans 6:14)…
Then what is tithing now?
Command… or principle?
This is where many people get uncomfortable.
Because the New Testament does not command believers to give 10%.
You won’t find a single direct instruction saying, “Christians must tithe.”
Instead, you find something deeper. Harder. More exposing.

2 Corinthians 9:7 —
“Each one must give as he has decided in his heart, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.”
No percentage.
No fixed demand.
No legal pressure.
But don’t relax too quickly… because this actually raises the standard.
Under the Law, you could calculate your obedience.
Under grace, God examines your heart.
You can hit 10% and still be far from Him.
You knew that.
God saw it.
You gave, but your heart stayed closed. You checked a box, but never surrendered your life.
And Jesus addressed that spirit directly.

In Luke 11:42, He said,
“You give a tenth… but you neglect justice and the love of God. You should have practiced the latter without leaving the former undone.”
Do you see it?
Tithing wasn’t the issue. The heart was.
Because God has never been after your money.
He’s after you.
This is where everything turns.

In the New Covenant, giving is no longer about meeting a requirement…
It’s about reflecting a transformation.
Because when grace actually grips you—when you realize what Christ has done—you don’t ask, “What’s the minimum I can give?”
You start asking, “What is my life worth in response to this?”
And that question will confront you.
Because grace isn’t cheap.

2 Corinthians 8:9 —
“For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sake he became poor, so that you through his poverty might become rich.”
He didn’t give 10%.
He gave everything.
His body. His blood. His life.
So now you stand in that tension.
Not under compulsion… but under calling.
Not forced… but exposed.
Because here’s the truth most won’t say out loud:
Some people hide behind “we’re under grace” as an excuse to give nothing.
Others cling to tithing as a way to feel righteous without surrendering their hearts.
Both miss it.
Completely.
One withholds. The other substitutes.
But the Gospel calls you into something deeper than both.

Romans 12:1 —
“Present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God—this is your true worship.”
Not just your money.
Your life.
So is tithing a command?
Not under the New Covenant.
Is it a principle?
Yes—but not as a ceiling.
As a starting point for a surrendered heart.
And this is where it becomes real for you.
Because you already know what your giving reveals.
You’ve felt that hesitation.
That internal negotiation.
That moment where generosity collided with fear.
And you pulled back.
God saw it.
This isn’t about guilt.
It’s about truth.
Because the issue isn’t whether you give 10%.
The issue is whether Jesus actually owns you.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
There are two paths in front of you right now.
One where you continue giving selectively, safely, comfortably—never truly trusting God, never fully surrendered.
And another where your heart breaks open under grace… and your giving becomes worship, not obligation.
Not measured by percentage.
But by surrender.
And if you stay here—if you keep wrestling with truth instead of running from it—you’ll start to see what real discipleship looks like beyond surface religion.
Not just content… but correction, depth, and clarity that cuts through confusion like this.
Say it.
Even if it’s uncomfortable.
Even if it’s just, “I’ve been giving, but not surrendered.”
Or, “I’ve been holding back.”
Let it come into the light.
Follow if you’re done with shallow teaching and want truth that actually transforms.
And if you’re ready to go deeper—to be challenged, corrected, and discipled in truth that doesn’t compromise—step into it here:
Because this isn’t about money.
It never was.
It’s about whether your life belongs to Jesus.
